articles.title: IRGC Navy says two 'violating' oil tankers hit naval mine in Hormuz Strait
articles.summary:
IRGC Navy says two 'violating' oil tankers hit naval mine in Hormuz Strait

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said that two "offending" oil tankers on the southern and eastern coasts of the Strait of Hormuz suffered explosions. 

"These tankers, believing they were secretly trying to pass through the fake Strait of Hormuz route, were prevented from passing by naval mines, causing a massive explosion and fire," it said in a statement. 

"We warn all crews of ships with navigation and positioning systems turned off, be careful not to let the lies of American officials lead you to the explosion and fire of naval mines," the IRGC added.

articles.title: Infants hardest hit as meningitis cases continue to rise in Gaza
articles.summary: Infants are bearing the brunt of a continued rise in meningitis cases in the Gaza Strip, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday, reporting more than 533 cases and four deaths since mid-October, Anadolu reports. WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier told reporters in Geneva that the agency and Gaza’s Health Ministry are closely monitoring the situation, with cases increasing rapidly between mid- and late October and “have continued to rise since.” Children under the age of one account for 71% of cases reported since October, with newborns alone accounting for 13% of all cases, he said. articles.title: Iran blacklists 26 tugboats operating in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran blacklisted 26 tugboats operating in the Strait of Hormuz for providing services to vessels using an alternative southern route through the strategic waterway, Anadolu reports. The Gulf Waterway Management Authority, an Iranian body established to regulate vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, announced the measure Tuesday in a statement on the US social media platform X. The authority said the decision followed reports received from individuals living in countries south of Iran, as well as field monitoring that it said showed the tugboats were assisting ships using the alternative southern route through the strait. articles.summary: Trump administration officials are internally debating whether the US military should target senior Iranian leaders to remove hard-liners and bring the nine-month Iran war to an end, NBC News reported Tuesday, Anadolu reports. Citing a US official and a person familiar with the discussions, the report said supporters argue such operations could demonstrate Washington’s ability to locate and kill Iranian leaders at will, giving US President Donald Trump an off-ramp to conclude the war. However, opponents within the administration and military warned that leadership strikes could cause remaining Iranian officials to dig in, damage US credibility in future peace talks and expose American personnel to heightened retaliation.
